name: Modern SEO M2 L2: GBP Landing Page Audit and Optimization
body:
> Module 2, 10:36 (speech ends at about 7:11; the rest is a silent, frozen screen). Source: Lesson 2 GBP Landing Page Audit and Optimization.mp4

## In short
- Step 2 of the low competition ranking method: make the website page the GBP links to (usually the homepage) match the GBP.
- Do the landing page review a few days after the GBP review, once the client has confirmed the final categories and services.
- Title tag and H1 should include the primary category and the city. He prefers the category first and the brand name at the end, within 60 characters.
- Check NAP (name, address, phone) on the page and in the footer, LocalBusiness schema, location content, a GBP map embed, a reviews embed, and clickable phone links.
- Add content, do not delete what is already ranking. Only remove thin parts like a bare list of cities.

## Key ideas
- **Order matters.** GBP review first, client confirms categories and services, then a few days later the landing page review. The page needs the final categories before it can be aligned. (0:37)
- **Title tag.** The primary category should be in it. The demo site's title led with the business name ("Right Way Driving School | We help you drive", shown in the browser tab). He would put "driving school" as the first two words, add the city (Cedar Grove), move the brand to the end, and use AI to fit it within 60 characters. (1:12 to 1:53)
- **H1.** Same rule: include the primary category and the city. The demo H1 was just "Right Way Driving School", so it needs a rewrite. (1:53 to 2:23)
- **NAP match.** The phone on the site matched the GBP. The address (83 East Lindsley Road) was not on the site, and the footer had no name, address or phone. (2:23 to 2:55)
- **Schema.** Run the page through a schema markup validator. The demo page had no schema, so correct LocalBusiness schema needs to be written and added. (3:26)
- **Location content.** Normally this talks about the target city. Because this client's target was a "near me" search, he wants content about the region around Cedar Grove and how they serve it. A plain list of cities "isn't really the type of content that works" and is thin. (3:26 to 4:33)
- **GBP embed.** Search the business in Google Maps, click Share, then "Embed a map", and copy the iframe code onto the page. (4:33)
- **Reviews.** Add a Google reviews or testimonials embed, separate from the map. The client had 385 reviews and none were shown on the page. (5:04)
- **Clickable phone links.** All phone numbers should be tap-to-call (tel: links). The demo site's were not. (5:04)
- **Do not delete working content.** The client already ranks fairly well, so he would only remove the city list and add new content (secondary categories, core services, geography) using a Claude writing prompt. (5:43 to 6:47)

## Step-by-step process
1. Wait until the client has approved the GBP categories and services from Lesson 1. (0:37)
2. Check the title tag. Does it include the primary category and the city? Rewrite with category and city first and brand at the end, within 60 characters. (1:12 to 1:53)
3. Check the H1. Rewrite it to include the primary category and the city. (1:53 to 2:23)
4. Compare the phone number on the page with the GBP. (2:23)
5. Compare the address on the page with the GBP. Add it if missing. (2:55)
6. Check the footer for name, address and phone. (2:55)
7. Copy the page URL into a schema markup validator (Fetch URL) and check for LocalBusiness schema. (3:26)
8. Review the location content. Does it really talk about the city or region served, or is it a thin list of towns? (3:26 to 4:33)
9. Check for a GBP map embed. If missing, get the code from Google Maps (search the business, Share, Embed a map) and paste it into the review document. (4:33)
10. Check for a Google reviews or testimonials embed. (5:04)
11. Check that phone links are clickable. (5:04)
12. Send the results to the client, get permission, then pass the fixes to the developer. (5:04 to 5:43)
13. Use the Claude writing prompt to add content about secondary categories, core services and the geography. Keep existing content that works. (5:43 to 6:47)

## Checklist
- Client has confirmed final GBP categories and services
- Title tag includes primary category and city, brand at the end, 60 characters or less
- H1 includes primary category and city
- Name, address and phone on the page exactly match the GBP
- Name, address and phone in the footer
- LocalBusiness schema present and matching the GBP NAP
- Unique content about the location or region served (not just a list of cities)
- GBP map embed on the page
- Google reviews or testimonials embed on the page, separate from the map
- All phone links clickable (tel: links)
- Client permission received before the developer makes changes
- Existing content that ranks is kept; new content is added

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| GBP Review document, "On-Site" table | Records each landing page check with Result and Suggestion | 0:37, 3:26 |
| AI (for title tags) | Writing a title tag within the 60 character limit | 1:12 |
| Schema markup validator ("structured data testing tool", Fetch URL) | Checking whether the page has schema | 3:26 |
| Google Maps Share, Embed a map | Getting the GBP map iframe code | 4:33 |
| Claude writing prompt | Rewriting and expanding the GBP landing page content | 5:43 |
| Rank map | Confirms the client is already ranking reasonably, so nothing working gets deleted | 6:16 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
- Title tag limit: 60 characters. (1:12)
- The client has 385 reviews. (5:04)
- He describes it as a "seven minute GBP landing page review." (6:47)
- "When these changes are made, we will see the rank map get better, almost guaranteed." Instructor claim, not verified. (6:47)

## Terms
**GBP landing page:** The web page the Google Business Profile links to. Usually the homepage.
**NAP:** Name, address and phone number. Must match the GBP exactly.
**LocalBusiness schema:** Structured data code that tells Google the business type and its address and phone, matching the GBP.
**GBP embed map:** A Google Maps iframe of the business placed on the landing page.
**Title tag:** The page title shown in search results and the browser tab.
**H1:** The main heading on the page.

## Worth quoting
- "We want to include the primary category and city name." (1:53)
- "I'm not going to delete stuff that's working." (6:47)
- "This is just a list of cities." (3:58)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Find each client's GBP landing page first.** Check which URL each GBP (Pipeliners, Alphalete, Summit AZ) links to, then run this checklist on that page.
- **Title tags and H1s.** Check whether each landing page title and H1 include the primary category and city. For Alphalete, titles and meta descriptions are set in Search Atlas (Metasync), not Yoast (memory file `project_alphalete_blog_yoast_format.md`). Alphalete also has a known site-wide second H1 from the copy-delete-posts plugin overlay (memory file `project_alphalete_duplicate_h1.md`), which matters for the H1 check.
- **Phone match on Summit AZ.** Summit uses GHL dynamic number insertion. Browsers may show pool tracking numbers, while the HTML, schema and tel: links keep the real number (480) 447-7008 (memory file `feedback_summit_ghl_dni.md`). Check the page source, not just the screen, and never disable the DNI snippet.
- **Schema check.** Run each landing page through a schema validator. On Summit AZ the mu-plugin outputs Plumber and LocalBusiness schema only on "Service in City" pages (memory file `project_summit_location_seo_mu.md`), so the homepage needs its own check. On Alphalete, the helper mu-plugin outputs no standalone LocalBusiness node (memory file `project_alphalete_duplicate_h1.md`).
- **Map and reviews embeds, clickable phones, footer NAP.** Check each one and list what is missing.
- **Write it up for Kim.** Client sites are read-only for Claude, so the output is a fix list (page, current value, proposed value) for Kim to apply or hand to a developer.
- **Add, don't delete.** Follow the lesson's rule on pages that already rank: replace only thin parts such as bare city lists, and add content.

## Open questions
- At 2:55 the transcript says "They don't have the phone number on their website," but the screen shows the phone in the top bar and hero, and the document entry is "Add address to website." He most likely meant the address.
- At 1:53 "driving school Cedar Grove right way driving school is not the title tag" is garbled. It seems to mean that exact wording is not required, only that the primary category and city are included (unclear in video).
- The tool at 3:26 is called "structured data testing tool. Mark up validator" in the transcript; the browser tab reads "Schema..." so it is likely the Schema Markup Validator (unclear in video).
- The audit template's "Recommended landing page", "Recommended H1" and "Recommended Title Tag" boxes (seen in Lesson 1) were not filled in on screen.
- The video runs from about 7:11 to 10:33 with no speech and a frozen screen, then a fragment of the intro repeats at 10:33. Nothing appears to be missing, but the end may have been cut badly.
- "Almost guaranteed" improvement is an unverified claim.
- No low-confidence lines in the manifest.

## Timestamps
- 0:04 Intro: step 2, the landing page connected to the GBP
- 0:37 Why the landing page review comes after GBP approval
- 1:12 Title tag: primary category first, brand last, 60 characters
- 1:53 City in the title tag, then the H1
- 2:23 H1 rewrite and phone number check
- 2:55 Address missing, footer NAP missing
- 3:26 Schema check, location content
- 3:58 Thin city list, expanding geographic content
- 4:33 How to get the GBP embed code
- 5:04 Reviews embed, clickable phone links, sending to client
- 5:43 Permission, developer, Claude content prompt
- 6:16 Keep what's working, only add content
- 6:47 Wrap-up
